title: Roast Chicken
subtitle: Classic roast chicken with crispy skin and herb butter
excerpt: A whole chicken roasted until the skin is deeply golden and crackling, the flesh is juicy to the bone, and the juices in the roasting tin become the base for a simple but perfect pan gravy.

recipe.sourceNotes: Roast chicken is one of the foundational dishes of home cooking across European culture. It is considered the benchmark of a cook's skill in France, where the legendary phrase attributed to chef Fernand Point states that to judge a cook you need only taste their roast chicken. A well-roasted chicken is not a complicated dish, but it requires attention to a few key principles: a hot oven, a dry skin, fat under the skin or all over to promote browning, and accurate resting time. The bird must rest after roasting for the juices to redistribute into the flesh: a chicken cut immediately on coming from the oven will lose its juice on the board. The pan juices and residue left in the roasting tin after resting are the basis of a pan sauce or gravy that requires almost no effort and reflects the concentrated flavour of the roasting process. The lemon inside the cavity creates steam from the inside as the bird cooks.

recipeTools.notes: A roasting tin large enough to hold the chicken with space around it.

content.text: Dry the chicken skin thoroughly with kitchen paper before roasting: moisture on the skin produces steam and prevents browning. Roasting at a high temperature for the whole time, rather than starting high and reducing, produces a more evenly browned bird. Rest the chicken for at least 15 minutes after roasting before carving: this is not optional. For the pan gravy, tip the tin on the hob, add a splash of wine or stock to the juices, and scrape all the caramelised bits from the base.

items.preparation: about a 1.8 kg bird; dried well with kitchen paper
2 for the cavity, 2 for the tin
or stock, for the pan gravy

content.text: Remove the chicken from the fridge 30 minutes before cooking. Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7. Mix the softened butter with a little salt, pepper, and the leaves from 2 thyme sprigs. Ease the skin away from the breast and push the butter underneath. Rub the outside with oil and season generously.

Put the halved lemon, garlic, and remaining thyme inside the cavity. Place the chicken breast-side up in the roasting tin. Roast for 60 to 70 minutes (allow 25 minutes per kg plus 20 minutes) until the juices run clear when the thigh is pierced and the skin is deeply golden.

Lift the chicken onto a board and rest for 15 minutes, loosely covered. Meanwhile, tip the roasting tin onto the hob over medium heat. Add the wine and scrape up the brown bits. Bubble for 2 minutes. Strain into a warm jug for the gravy. Carve and serve.
